Title: Two-Factor Authentication Setup
FAQ: How do I set up two-factor authentication?

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security to your account. To enable 2FA, go to Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication and click Enable. We support authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy) and SMS verification. Authenticator apps are recommended over SMS for stronger security. After enabling 2FA, you will be prompted for a verification code at each login.

What is multi-factor authentication and how does it add a layer of security by requiring two or more credentials?

**Summary:**

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of security to accounts by requiring two or more credentials to authenticate. This typically involves a combination of something you **know** (password) and something you **have** (authentication app, physical token).

**How it works:**

- When you enable MFA, you'll be prompted to provide two different credentials at login.
- One credential is typically something you **know**, like a password or PIN.
- The other is something you **have**, such as an authentication app like Google Authenticator or a physical token like a security key.

**Benefits of MFA:**

- Adds an extra layer of security by requiring multiple credentials.
- Makes it more difficult for attackers to gain access to your account even if they have stolen one of your credentials.

**Common MFA methods:**

- **Authentication apps:** Generate time-based codes that change regularly.
- **Physical tokens:** Hardware devices that generate one-time codes.
- **SMS verification:** Receive a code via text message to your mobile phone.

**Conclusion:**

MFA is an effective way to enhance the security of your accounts by requiring two or more credentials to authenticate. It is highly recommended to enable MFA for added protection against unauthorized access.
